reviews.comment: Best. Professor. Ever.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: I took CHEN 205 with Dr. Holtzapple in Scotland and it was frankly the best learning experience of my life. Dr. Holtzapple was experienced and taught concepts like entropy and reversibility extremely well, and was amazing and accessible outside of class. Very caring and made the exams understandable and easy, amazing professor and experience!

CHEN201 is not a necessary class for chemical engineering, in my opinion. It is merely a review of basic principles of mathematics/physics that you already had an idea of before taking the class. The Excel stuff is helpful, though. Exams are online and multiple choice(no partial credit). They are nothing like the homework as well. Good luck.
Gave a lot of pop quizzes and group homework.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: 90% of this class is a waste of time in my opinion. Having lectures 3x a week is absurd, as Holtzapple normally just spends it rambling on off topic subjects. Other than that, the exams don't take that much studying, and an A is feasible for most students as long as you just show up and do the in class quizzes. 2

Pros: Holtzapple is good for advice, industry wisdom. Lots of interesting topics covered. 
Cons: Class is very poorly organized, no canvas usage. Materials can be hard to find. Too many pop quizzes, class expectations are wayyy too high. IMO class needs to be completely reworked and introduced in freshman year for 2 or 3 credit hours.

Holtzapple does make this class an unnecessary headache. He does warn you that this one hour class will feel like three and that is very accurate. It's unavoidable to have him most likely, so you just have to get through it. Show up to class to take the RATs (quizzes over reading) and take a moment to read over the slides or textbook right before

Be prepared to read his textbooks for RAT assignments at the beginning of every chapter, and be aware of his exams, as he'll traumatize you from learning through failure. Also, you should talk to him after class. He has many interesting stories, especially his inclusion in big industries like Shell, and his inventions that he's eager to present.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Holtzapple made this class way more of a headache than it needed to be. He made it so everything had to be turned in on paper, and his lectures sometimes made me wonder why I was even there. He was actually a pretty good teacher, but the organization of the class was very disappointing. I'm sure he would be much better for other CHEN classes.
reviews.ratingTags: Group projects--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Dr. Holtzapple is a good professor who knows his stuff. The class is interesting and it's a good survey of stuff you should know for CHEN, however, credit hour to work ratio is absurd. 1 credit hour for such an insane amount of busy work is absurd. However, Dr. Holtzapple is good, and if you put time and work into this class, you will learn well.

You will definitely be learning on your own for the exam, lecture mostly have nothing to do with exam, daily rat quizzes for classes so attendance will basically be mandatory, every lecture you will have hw to do. Exam is open notes/ open internet but you will still avg the class with a 70 on exams, no curve but you get a bonus exam for some points

201 with Holtzapple had to be one of my poorest college experiences. The class was worth 1 credit hour yet we met 3 times a week. Insane amounts of homework that took hours upon hours to complete. The test had averages in the 50-60 and he had to curve due to how bad the scores were. The class has gone through a lot of revisions due to this.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Amazing professor and industry genius. His class is hard and tedious but he gives you a LOT of opportunities to get an A, learn from mistakes, get points back, and get extra credit. He is blunt but wants you to learn. Bonus exams to raise your grade.

Dr. Holtzapple is the most passionate professor I've ever had. His lectures are pretty good and he cares a lot about his students. The only downside is the amount of work there is for just a 1 credit hour class, but that will happen regardless of the professor. There is lots of extra credit and it's easy to get an A if you do the assignments.

Holtzapple is the sweetest prof. He genuinely cares about the material he teaches as well as the improvement of the class. His passion makes up his teaching discrepancies, and he offers bonus tests to improve your exam grades. If you put in the effort, you will definitely succeed with him.

Dr. Holtzapple is the most passionate prof I have ever had. While CHEN 201 may not be my favorite of his creations (there is way too much content for just 1 credit hour), he makes it fair and enjoyable. I wish we were given more time in class for work (for example, on our final) because again, it is a one credit hour class.

Holtzapple is a great prof. His lecturing skills aren't the best, but he is very passionate and communicates key points. There is so much extra credit available on exams and other assignments that it's hard to not get an A. The class is a lot of work for a 1 hour course, but never causes stress. he is also very nice and accessible outside of class!
reviews.ratingTags: EXTRA CREDIT--Group projects--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Dr. Holtzapple was a very caring professor. He gave many opportunities for extra credit, and was an incredibly effective lecturer. CHEN 201 is mostly comprised of content covered in other classes, but Dr. Holtzapple's teaching style provides the push necessary to make them 'click' in the context of engineering. Super friendly, super accessible!
Creepy with bad lectures

This class is hard because Holtzapple wants to ensure you actually learn the content given to you. If the majority of the class has trouble understanding a concept, he will test on it again and again. He gives a lot of extra credit opportunity and if you put the work in you will do well in his class. Homeworks are hard and take a few hours.
reviews.ratingTags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: If you're just looking for an A, there are better options. However, if you're looking to LEARN, Dr. Holtzapple is the man. He'll force you to truly think like a real world engineer to be successful and he's very intentional in actually helping you learn w/o letting you get discouraged. He gave plenty of EC opportunities for those that struggled.

Professor Holtzapple is my favorite professor. He cares so much about his students, and yes his class is difficult, but he gives you every opportunity to bounce back. Attend review sessions, office hours, and engage with the notes. We ended up having a bonus exam for every exam, and we had 6 extra credit points that we could get added to our grade.

The way his class was structured, I learned nothing. The first third of the class is just review so you have to learn a semester's worth of content in 2/3 the time. Often the stuff taught in class would never be brought up again. It's a tough class and it feels like he goes out of his way to make it harder/ more inconvenient.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: On the one hand, Dr. Holtzapple truly cares about making sure you become a great chemical engineer. However, the majority of his lecture focuses on conceptual concepts and makes us do homework problems which he states don't help us prepare for the exams. Furthermore, the exams are from 7:00 pm to 11:00 pm (which I extremely dislike).
just horrible. no partial credit, not nice at all, and lectures were NOT helpful AT ALLL
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Holtzapple's lectures are very interactive and I learned a lot. His exams are very difficult, especially the final because we only had 2 hours. No partial credits on the exams, but each major question is broken down into smaller parts, and each part can worth anywhere from 1 to 7 points, so you get "partial credits" in that sense.

Holtzapple is okay for Thermo I. His lectures go really in depth, he really wants you to understand the concepts. He applies the content to real world examples which is really good, however if you don't understand certain things the way he does you might struggle. Exams are absurd and take a full 4 hours with many small parts but no partial credit.

People will say he's the one to get if you want to learn but I really didn't learn much from him. His lectures aren't really useful for the exams and I pretty much stopped going after a while. Exams are insanely long, 4+ hours, open internet, open notes, etc but fairly hard. Curves exam averages to a 75, but you'll need it.

One of the best professors in Chemical Engineering. He values intuition, clear communication, and giving you problems that line up with the concepts and although his test questions can be unorthodox, they are always interesting and the methods you use are not theory heavy. He is the only reason I haven't dropped out of CHEN

If you're taking this over the summer, be prepared to be very busy! Exams are very difficult (averages around 50s and 60s) but will be curved. Mainly goes over theory and basic concepts during lecture but will be referenced on exams. Plenty of homework assignments and a paper at the end of the term, but they are completed with teams. Good luck lol
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Group projects

reviews.comment: Dr. Holtzapple is a phenomenal instructor. His mixed ratings make complete sense because his teaching style is different from typical classes. His lectures are all theory-based and focus on concepts. His tests are the application of the concepts. They are VERY HARD! But he curves to a 75, with low averages, so lots of points back. I Would recommend

No partial credit so good luck. Exams are way more difficult than they should be. You think you understand some of it but fail. Class averages on the exams are 50-60% while other classes are 80%+. TAKE SOMEONE ELSE.
reviews.ratingTags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I would recommend another professor. He intentionally makes the exams different from the hw and doesn't provide practice problems. No partial credit, if you get part a wrong and a is used in b you get b wrong. Lectures are theory with only basic examples given. Also mentions his own textbook frequently in addition to the required textbook.

Professor Holtzapple is a good lecturer and it is clear he is passionate about the thermo and his students. However, his tests are ridiculously difficult (online 3 hr test for about 50 math calculations that are double jeopardy, no curve) even though his lecture is only theory. Studying textbook problems and finding outside resources is a must.

This prof is a phenomenal teacher. However, In my opinion, His expectations for exams are way to high for undergraduates. Difficulty is hard which is fine but the questions are designed for you to be ridiculously fast at calculating. In industry, you have to think hard, but no one is going to ask you to calculate 60 different things in 3 hours.

Best professor in the department. Simple as that. Negative reviews are for 2 reasons. People will say his class is too hard, and may say that he has a short temper. His classes force you to actually think instead of being a human calculator. The short temper is reserved for people who don't try very hard then complain about it.

One of the last profs left in the dept that truly teaches fundamentals. Dr. Holtzapple will change how you solve problems forever. He brings so much energy into class you can't help but pay attention. He is by far the most dedicated professor I have ever encountered when it comes to teaching students. TAKE HIS CLASS!

A VERY negative person, he shamed me in the review for asking questions. No practice in lectures; purposefully makes exams diff from hw. His exam averages: 52, 69, 46. Does provide detailed economic background, but nothing but theory in his lectures. I felt uncomfortable because of his attitude, and switched to a diff prof for thermo 2.

He goes by the standard textbook that the chemical engineering department recommends but also advertises his book all throughout the semester. Honestly, I already paid for the class and was hoping he would give more information in class that could help us be successful in the course. He does not give practice problems for the tests so beware.

Don't do it dude... The exams are crazy and confusing with no partial credit. All conceptual lectures with very little examples or math which sucks since the work has to be perfect to receive any credit on exams that were timed and rushed.
3hr tests crammed into 1.25hrs.

I had Dr. Holtzapple for 204 & had a terrible experience with him. This class was a pleasant surprise. Even though I have never agreed with his testing style & never will, he taught Thermo II very well. It is definitely possible to make a B in the class; an A will take a lot of work. Of all the classes he teaches, he teaches this one the best.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Everyone says Mark Holtzapple is the hardest prof in the department, and while his 7hr tests can be grueling, you come away from them having learned more. He really cares about the subject and relates it to industry, so you wont be wasting time on theory. Overall he was tough, but if you value your education, there's no better choice.

Dr. Holtzapple is very knowledgeable of the engineering world. His 7-hour exams are written so that you learn to prevent any mistakes you would naturally make in your career with relation to the class. However, his Final Exams are incredibly more difficulty because of the 2 hour time limit, lack of clarity, and mismatching units with quantities.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Best professor I have ever had in CHEN so far. He teaches and mentors you to become a successful engineer in industry and not only at academia. He is devoted to his students. He is awesome!

Definitely the best professor in the CHEN department that I've seen, likely the best prof in the whole university. He cares tremendously about his job and his students. He teaches/mentors you to become an engineer that truly knows what is going on. If you aren't in love with the major, don't take him. But if you are, absolutely take him.

Dr. Holtzapple is very intelligent, but he is not very effective when teaching. His lectures are not representative of the open-book portion of exams. He can teach concepts all day long, but he falls extremely short in teaching the math behind the concepts, which doesn't make much sense when the majority of the exams involve math. Do not take him.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: If you want to be a top-notch engineer then you need to take Holtzapple. He took thermodynamics, normally an excessively boring and difficult subject, and made it come alive. He cares about every student and checks regularly to make sure everyone's on the same page. He takes all questions, and teaches useful things that aren't taught anywhere else.

Dr. Holtzapple has open internet tests. They're are hard and have "unlimited time", but he always calls it at around 3am (they start at 7pm.) I enjoyed his tests because they took the pressure off and the problems were really cool. His class isn't for everyone, but I'm taking him for thermo II because he is an amazing teacher who cares a lot.
Don't take him. You'll regret it if you do.

plain and simple. if you dont love chemical engineering you will hate him/the class. sure the tests are hard: they are legit open internet/textbook/notes with unlimited time but nothing like the hw. but heads up OUR REAL JOBS WILL (probably) BE NOT LIKE THE HW. he teaches practical lessons that Ill need to know and he does want you to do well.

One of the few CHEN profs to actually care about whether or not we're learning. The class itself is insanely difficult but he tries to make it as fair as possible. Exams don't have a time limit and he gives a lot of opportunity for extra credit. Go to class and actually pay attention and you should do well enough.

Class is very difficult, but he will teach you things outside of the regular curriculum he thinks you need to know to be successful. Tests have no time limit. Open book/internet section but don't be fooled they're still painfully hard. He curves the median to a 75 for each test. He is a genius and if you care more about learning than GPA take him.

Dr. Holtzapple is intelligent and wants all engineers to have a complete understanding of the material, so his tests require a deep understanding of the material. His tests are super unorthodox in the fact that they don't have a time limit and the questions wont resemble anything you've ever seen before. The class is doable, but get ready to work.

Dr. Holtzapple is an amazing professor, and you will learn a lot of practical things in his class. His exams require critical thinking, so if all you do is plug and chug you will not do well on his exams. The only reason you would ever stay late for his exam is if you didn't truly understand the material he taught.
His exams have no time limit, so you will be there until 3am at the earliest. The exam starts at 7pm. It is the most impractical thing I've ever seen a professor do.

DO NOT TAKE HIM. His tests are nothing like the hw and he even tells you that. They are so much more difficult than anything taught in class. He does no examples in class and his tests are almost impossible. He has no time limit for his tests so youll probs be there till like 3 am. Do not take him if you want to keep your sanity.

Dr. Holtzapple truly wants you to learn. He understands that in industry you are not going to use what you learned and tries to teach you the most important aspects to take away. His tests are difficult so you truly need to study for them. The first half is vocabulary with true and false while the second half is problem solving. I learned a lot.
